monthly_review.summary: You've increased volume and intensity this month, with faster paces and higher HR — a clear step toward greater aerobic capacity, though efficiency and zone balance show trade-offs.
monthly_review.highlight: Your cadence increased by 5 spm while aerobic efficiency improved — indicating more economical running despite higher average HR and pace.

goal_tracker.message: You’ve already exceeded last month’s total distance by 8.5 km and matched the number of runs — no additional sessions or distance are needed to beat May’s totals.

insights.title: Efficiency gain despite faster pacing
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.42 to 13.55 while avg pace improved by 12 sec/km and avg HR increased 4 bpm — suggesting better neuromuscular coordination and oxygen utilization at higher intensities.

insights.title: Shift toward higher-intensity zones
insights.body: Zone 3 time increased from 19% to 28%, Zone 4 from 3% to 14%, and Zone 1 dropped from 36% to 26% — indicating reduced easy-run emphasis and potential under-recovery if sustained.

insights.title: Cadence-stride length trade-off evident
insights.body: Cadence rose +5 spm (146 → 151), but stride length in recent long runs (e.g., 69.52 cm on 6/16) is ~10 cm shorter than your fastest-effort run (91.13 cm on 6/11), suggesting form shifts with fatigue or intensity.

insights.title: High aerobic TE concentrated in long runs
insights.body: Three of your five recent runs (6/11, 6/16, 6/21) delivered aerobic TE ≥3.1 — all >10 km or with elevated HR — confirming effective stimulus, but absence of low-TE recovery runs (e.g., <2.0) may limit adaptation.

recommendations.action: Do one 45-min Zone 1 run (HR ≤125 bpm) before June ends — aim for cadence ≥145 spm and vertical oscillation ≤7.0 cm.
recommendations.reason: Your Zone 1 time dropped to 26% (vs 36% last month), and recent low-HR run (6/19) showed high ground contact (344 ms) and low efficiency — a dedicated easy run will support recovery and form refinement.

recommendations.action: On your next medium run (5–7 km), hold cadence ≥155 spm while keeping pace between 9:00–9:30 min/km (540–570 sec/km) and HR ≤142 bpm.
recommendations.reason: You achieved 162 spm at 6:32 min/km (6/11), but cadence dipped to 145–153 in longer efforts — reinforcing rhythm at sustainable intensities improves efficiency and reduces vertical oscillation drift.

recommendations.action: After your next run >8 km, perform 3 × 1-min strides (90 sec walk recovery) focusing on light ground contact (<280 ms) and vertical oscillation <6.5 cm — use Garmin’s real-time metrics if available.
recommendations.reason: Ground contact time averaged 314–322 ms in long runs vs 274 ms in your fastest effort; targeted neuromuscular priming can improve spring-like recoil and stride efficiency.

weekly_focus.description: Balance newly gained speed and efficiency with intentional low-intensity work and neuromuscular reinforcement to solidify gains without accumulating fatigue.
suggested_sessions: 5–6 km tempo run with cadence ≥155 spm
